# Correlated scalar metadata stages

This reference records the independent Spark fields and rows used by
[#818](https://github.com/mag1cfrog/delta-arrow-reader/issues/818). It is for
maintainers replaying or recapturing the metadata boundary. Scalar naming
[#790](https://github.com/mag1cfrog/delta-arrow-reader/issues/790) and nested
outer-field resolution #819 are separate work.

`scope-spark.jsonl` contains a header and 36 observations from Spark 4.2.0,
revision `32f7299601108917fb01920a54e084595b7b3bf8`, in UTC. Each of six queries
runs in both ANSI modes against populated, NULL-only and empty providers.
`original-scope-spark.jsonl` is the unchanged 24-observation prefix, including
its header. The last 12 records add explicit inner STRUCT and direct-column
aliases. Both capture scripts are unchanged from the independent capture.
`manifest.json` records their hashes and the two existing fixture dependencies.

The complete corpus SHA256 is
`5d05c103ece4c6b5df6cb5ef48d20fcfd970d01e981b2e3bd73844a66779def2`.
The preserved prefix SHA256 is
`332f7962d37366265ff8b23c0b170c40e1b451a4fff04ef67933a8ad0c3b3d5c`.
Plans and every recorded schema stage remain in the raw files. Rows are sorted
for comparison without removing duplicates.

The tests compare the public fields to `public_schema`, the physical fields to
`executed_schema_after_collect`, and all rows to `expected.rows`. They also
check that the recorded analyzed/public and optimized/executed stages agree,
and validate each returned Arrow batch against its physical schema. Metadata,
names, nested types and nullability are compared exactly at each stage.

For the nullable `q.v` source carrying `source=plain`, the correlated queries
require these differences:

| Inner SELECT expression | Public child metadata | Executed child metadata | Executed outer `r` metadata |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `STRUCT(q.v AS renamed)` | `{}` | `source=plain` | `__autoGeneratedAlias=true` |
| `STRUCT(q.v AS renamed) AS inner_s` | `{}` | `source=plain` | `{}` |
| `q.v AS inner_v` | No struct child | No struct child | `source=plain` |

The direct, POSITIVE and unary-positive nested-child queries remain passing
controls. They protect the existing distinction between analysis and execution
when source metadata returns after simplification. The corpus also retains the
required direct `id` output. Correlated required-source metadata is not covered
by these 36 records; existing scalar nonnullable and error guards remain active.

Run the complete metadata target from the standalone Spark SQL workspace:

```sh
cd crates/delta-arrow-reader-spark-sql
cargo +1.96.0 test --locked --workspace --test generated_alias_metadata -- --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

The new test performs 72 complete comparisons at batch sizes 1 and 32. The
test-only commit retains all production source from prerequisite
`5bce7951cf8665b9a6d44c1c57d36a8425fc83af`. That prerequisite is unmerged;
passing this target does not complete #710, #790 or #818.

To recapture in a pre-existing Spark 4.2.0 environment, stage the original
scripts and their dependencies in a temporary directory. Run from this fixture
directory. Use fresh output paths; the scripts refuse to overwrite a capture.

```sh
capture_dir=$(mktemp -d)
cp capture_struct_child_stages.py capture_struct_child_stages_v2.py original-scope-spark.jsonl "$capture_dir/"
cp ../struct-expression-names-spark.jsonl ../capture_floating_group_keys_spark.py "$capture_dir/"
python "$capture_dir/capture_struct_child_stages.py" "$capture_dir/seed-recapture.jsonl"
python "$capture_dir/capture_struct_child_stages_v2.py" "$capture_dir/complete-recapture.jsonl"
```

The v2 script copies the frozen seed bytes before appending the two inner-alias
queries. Its output intentionally uses `original-scope-spark.jsonl`, not the
new seed recapture. Compare fields and rows when assessing a new capture; Spark
plan expression IDs can vary between runs. Do not replace the committed raw
references with DAR output or normalize their metadata to make tests pass.
